accepted_units.title: Recursive Hopf structure turns composition data into an inverse operation
accepted_units.why_material: Generators and relations are equipped with a coproduct whose triangular recursion makes the antipode constructible as convolution inverse. The reusable move is to encode how a composite object splits, then obtain inversion or cancellation from the coalgebra rather than by ad hoc term manipulation.
accepted_units.context_note: The presentation is for the codimension-one transverse-geometry Hopf algebra; exact low-degree coproduct coefficients are formula-sensitive, but the recursive semantic mechanism is explicit.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the chosen generators Y, X, and delta_n for formulas, while the coproduct-plus-antipode pattern is representation-independent.

accepted_units.title: Dualization identifies Hopf coordinates with composition and inversion of formal diffeomorphisms
accepted_units.why_material: The source passes from a commutative coordinate Hopf algebra to the enveloping algebra of formal vector fields and then identifies the coordinate algebra with formal diffeomorphisms. Under this bridge, the antipode acquires the concrete semantic meaning of compositional inversion, showing how a difficult recursive algebraic operation becomes natural in a group representation.
accepted_units.context_note: The theorem-level identification is clear, although the intervening PBW calculations and displayed coordinate formulas contain glyph and layout risk and should not be copied coefficient-for-coefficient without the PDF.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The coordinate formulas depend strongly on the delta_n and jet bases; the duality and composition/inversion interpretation survives a change of coordinates.

accepted_units.title: Rooted trees encode nested and disjoint dependency structure
accepted_units.why_material: A nested dependency is represented by an edge toward the root and independent dependencies by separate branches. This compresses arbitrarily nested or disjoint subproblem structure into one generic combinatorial object and separates structural bookkeeping from the analytic expressions that motivated it.
accepted_units.context_note: The motivating functions are regularized integrals, but the accepted content is only the generic dependency-to-tree encoding; the displayed examples are partly figure-dependent.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Uses rooted trees as the chosen representation; the underlying distinction between nesting and disjointness is invariant under relabeling and independent of the QFT application.

accepted_units.title: Admissible cuts turn decomposition into a coproduct and recursive cancellation into an antipode
accepted_units.why_material: Root removal and grafting decompose and synthesize trees, while admissible cuts partition a tree into pruned branches and a rooted trunk. Summing these decompositions defines a coassociative coproduct, and recursive or all-cuts formulas define an antipode whose cancellation follows by pairing normal and full cuts with opposite sign.
accepted_units.context_note: Several small-tree examples are conveyed only by damaged figures, so the unit supports the definitions and proofs but not exact recovery of every pictured term.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The formulas use rooted trees and a distinguished root, but the move generalizes to recursively decomposable structures with compatible cuts.

accepted_units.title: Recursive subtraction remains valid across evaluations that preserve the obstructing part
accepted_units.why_material: Cuts induce nested brackets, and the antipode pairs an expression with its evaluated subtraction. Finiteness follows from cancellation in each normal/full-cut pair whenever the evaluation preserves the divergent part, yielding a reusable principle: isolate a bad component with a projection-like operation and organize recursive correction independently of the particular admissible evaluation scheme.
accepted_units.context_note: The claim is demonstrated on a renormalization toy model; acceptance concerns the abstract cancellation-under-preservation argument, not evaluation of the integrals or physical validity.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The bracket notation and divergence extractor are scheme-specific, whereas the preservation condition and paired recursive cancellation are structural.

accepted_units.title: A growth derivation exposes a structured subalgebra shared by two representations
accepted_units.why_material: Natural growth attaches a new vertex in all possible positions and acts derivationally on forests. Classifying how a cut interacts with the new edge gives a recursive coproduct relation and shows that the grown combinations form a closed Hopf subalgebra, thereby constructing a precise bridge from tree labels to the integer-indexed formal-diffeomorphism presentation.
accepted_units.context_note: Figure 13 is damaged, but the four-way cut classification and algebraic recurrence are recoverable from prose and formulas.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The growth operator is defined on rooted trees and the target uses indexed coordinates; the existence of a structure-preserving bridge, not the labels, is the reusable content.

accepted_units.title: Grafting reduces coassociativity to a recursive compatibility identity
accepted_units.why_material: The formal tree Hopf algebra is built from simple cuts. Instead of enumerating all double cuts directly, the proof introduces grafting L and establishes Delta composed with L equals L tensor 1 plus identity tensor L after Delta; induction then reduces coassociativity at the next degree to the previous degree. This is a reusable strategy for proving a global coherence law from a constructor-compatible local identity.
accepted_units.context_note: Dense tensor displays are somewhat layout-sensitive, but the proof architecture and the cut-to-grafting correspondence remain readable.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The proof is expressed through rooted-tree grafting, yet the constructor-compatibility induction applies to other recursively generated coalgebras.

accepted_units.title: A universal cocycle property characterizes the rooted-tree Hopf algebra
accepted_units.why_material: The grafting operator is recognized as a nontrivial Hochschild one-cocycle, and the pair consisting of the Hopf algebra and this cocycle is shown universal: every comparable pair receives a unique compatible Hopf morphism. The construction upgrades an example-dependent combinatorics into a canonical object specified by what maps out of it.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a theorem with an explicit inductive existence-and-uniqueness argument; exact cochain signs remain formula-sensitive in the normalized extraction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The rooted-tree model realizes the universal object, while the characterization by unique compatible morphisms is presentation-independent.

accepted_units.title: Single cuts dualize to insertion and an antisymmetric Lie bracket
accepted_units.why_material: Dualizing the commutative tree Hopf algebra yields an enveloping algebra whose primitive generators are indexed by trees. Counting single cuts defines an insertion-like product; symmetry of its associator makes antisymmetrization satisfy Jacobi, so decomposition data in the coproduct becomes synthesis data and a Lie bracket in the dual representation.
accepted_units.context_note: The proof is algebraically complete in the text, though long summations are extraction-sensitive and the source cautions that this operation is not the same as operadic transplantation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The cut counts and tree basis determine coefficients; the deeper decomposition-to-insertion duality does not depend on the physical decorations.

accepted_units.title: Extending the growth operator produces a quotient map to formal vector fields
accepted_units.why_material: The source derives how natural growth interacts with the coproduct, extends the Hopf and Lie structures by grading and translation generators, and constructs a surjective Lie homomorphism from the refined tree algebra to formal vector fields. This makes precise that the tree calculus refines, rather than merely resembles, the ordinary composition calculus.
accepted_units.context_note: The derivation identities are formula-dense, but the case split on whether the new edge is cut and the resulting structure-preserving map are readable.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The map forgets detailed tree shape through multiplicities and retains the formal-vector-field degree, explicitly exhibiting what the coarser representation preserves and forgets.

accepted_units.title: Characters convert recursive subtraction into group inversion and reduce work to primitives
accepted_units.why_material: Viewing the Hopf algebra as coordinates on a formal group identifies algebra characters with group-like elements. Inversion in this group reduces the full recursive subtraction problem to primitive inputs, illustrating how a representation change can isolate irreducible cases and synthesize all composite corrections.
accepted_units.context_note: The application sentence is stated for regularized Feynman diagrams, but the character-group and primitive-reduction mechanism is generic Hopf algebra mathematics.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Requires a suitable completion and a target coefficient field for characters; the reduction to primitive elements follows from the Hopf structure rather than the QFT interpretation.

accepted_units.title: Overlapping dependencies reduce to tree combinations plus enlarged primitive decorations
accepted_units.why_material: For an object with overlapping substructures, the source matches its reduced coproduct with that of a linear combination of rooted trees. Their difference is primitive, so the apparent extension is absorbed by enlarging the decoration set and recursing. The reusable move is to preserve the decomposition algebra while relocating irreducible residual complexity into primitive labels.
accepted_units.context_note: The argument is sketched and its detailed proof is deferred; the result should be treated as a supported construction outline, not a fully self-contained general theorem for arbitrary dependency systems.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The conclusion is internal to the specified Hopf-algebra conditions and decorated-tree representation; transfer to unrelated overlap systems requires independently checking the coproduct and primitive assumptions.
